CHARGE I, Samar Vishal, ASJ-08, West, Delhi, do hereby charge you the accused persons namely 1) Dinesh Pratap S/o Raj Pal Singh 2). Raj Pal Singh S/o Raghu Nandan Singh and 3). Kamla W/o Raj Pal Singh as under :-
That during the subsistence of marriage between you accused Dinesh Pratap S/o Raj Pal Singh and Vandana (since deceased) W/o Dinesh Pratap i.e. from 18.04.2018 till her death on 18.07.2019 at her matrimonial house i.e. E-100/3, Laxmi Park, Nangloi,
Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Nihal Vihar, all of you, in furtherance of your common intention, being the husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of Vandana (since deceased) subjected her to cruelty and harassment for not fulfilling the demand of Dowry and bringing sufficient dowry and thereby you all committed offence punishable u/s 498-A / 34 IPC within the cognizance of this Court.
Secondly, death of Vandana W/o Dinesh Pratap took place on 18.07.2019 i.e. within seven years of her marriage at her matrimonial house i.e. E-100/3, Laxmi Park, Nangloi, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Nihal Vihar and the same was otherwise than under normal circumstances and soon before her death, Vandana W/o Dinesh Pratap was subjected to cruelty and harassment by all of you, in furtherance of your common intention and in connection with demand of dowry and thereby all of you committed offence punishable u/s 304-B/34 IPC within the cognizance of Court of Session.
I hereby direct all of you to be tried by this Court for the above said offences.

After Vandana's marriage,

PW-4 Ankit Singh-Brother of deceaesd Vandana:
13. His sister Vandana was married to A-1 on 18.04.2018.
Before marriage, A-2 had demanded Rs. 25 lac as dowry.
His father gave A-2 Rs. 1.5 lac.
One month before the marriage, A-2 again demanded Rs. 10 lac but they could manage to pay only Rs. 6.5 lac.
His uncle helped his father with Rs. 7.5 lac.
In June, 2018 when Vandana visited their house, she told him that the accuseds used to torture her by saying that she had not given sufficient dowry.

6 14.
His cousin Vandana was married to A-1 on 18.04.2018.
In the evening of 18.07.2019, when he was in his house his mother received a call informing her that Vandana had died.
He along with his uncle Rajbir reached the matrimonial house of Vandana at Laxmi Park, Nangloi.
He found a crowd of neighbours gathered there and police officers present.
He went to the first floor of the house and there he found the dead body of his cousin Vandana kept in front of the room.
He entered the room and found three pieces of torn paper lying on the floor.
He found that some sentences were written on those pieces of paper and he noticed that those sentences were cut with the help of pen ink.
He handed over the said pieces of paper to IO SI Jai Bhagwan.
IO pasted the pieces of paper on a plain paper sheet and he signed that.

The said paper is Ex.PW-5/A which bears his signature at point A. DISCUSSION :
15.
Vandana was married to Dinesh Pratap.
Their marriage was solemnized on 18.04.2018.
On 18.07.2019, Vandana committed suicide by hanging.
She committed suicide in her matrimonial house.

She was last seen alive at about 3 p.m and she was found hanging at about 5 p.m. Consequent to her unnatural death, inquest proceedings were conducted by the SDM concerned and upon noting of SDM, present FIR was registered against Dinesh Pratap (A-1), Rajpal Singh (A-2) and Kamla (A-3).
A-1 was husband of the deceased -Vandana.
A-2 was father-in-law of the deceased.
A-3 was mother-in-law of deceased.
SDM considered case fit to be investigated by the police, on the basis of statements of the relatives of paternal family of Vandana.

16. Death report (Ex.PW-6/C) and postmortem report of deceased Vandana (Ex.AD5)
record that the cause of death of Vandana is asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
There were no injuries noticed.
During postmortem, blood and viscera were preserved for toxicological analysis.

The toxicological report (Ex.AD6) records that metallic poisons, ethyl and methyl alcohol, cyanide, phosphide, alkaloids, barbiturates, tranquilizers and pesticides were not detected in the blood and viscera of the deceased.
Ex.PW-6/C and Ex.AD5 do not record existence of any injury- external or internal, on the person of deceased.

16.1 From the above referred facts, it is inferred that before death, Vandana was not intoxicated/
poisoned and that she was not subjected to physical violence of any sorts.
It is also sufficiently established that Vandana's death was not caused by burns or bodily injury.

17. It is proved that death of Vandana occurred within seven years of her marriage and that her death occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances; the deceased was married to A-1 on 18.04.2018 and she died on 18.07.2019 and her death was caused by asphyxia due to ante-mortem hanging.

18. The only ingredient of the offence punishable u/s 304B IPC which the prosecution was burdened with to prove, to successfully bring home the charge u/s 304 B IPC, was that soon before her death,

18.1 PW-1/father of the deceased, deposed that there was no special reason for Vandana's suicide.

Pertinent portion of his examination-in-chief recorded on 23.11.2021 is reproduced below for ready reference:-
"There was no special reason for committing suicide by my daughter.
There was some family dispute between my daughter and Vinita, Kamla and Dinesh Pratap Singh"

18.2 The Ld. Addl. PP put leading questions to PW-1 and in reply thereto PW-1 deposed that he had deposed to the Executive Magistrate that in the month of December-2018, A-1 had demanded Rs. 3 lac for purchasing a vehicle.
But, there is no deposition to the effect that to coerce the deceased or her family to satisfy this demand, the deceased was subjected to cruelty.
Furthermore, Vandana committed suicide on 18.07.2019 and this day cannot be said to be 'soon after' December-2018.

The only fact which can be considered eligible to be an incident of some sort of harassment, as found in the contents of the deposition of PW-1 is reproduced below:-
"

It is correct that I had stated to the Executive Magistrate that prior to 20 days of the incident, I met my daughter Vandana, who told me that "meri saas mujhai kehti thi ki tujhai bachcha nahi ho sakta humai teri jarurat nahi hai"."
18.3 This conversation between PW-1 and Vandana, cited by PW-1 in the above quoted testimony is not in respect of dowry demand.
Furthermore, the use of the verb 'thi' is suggestive of the inference that A-3 had said this to Vandana not 'soon before' her death.
The auxiliary verb 'thi' is in past tense.
19. One of the arguments of the defence is that Vandana was not keeping well and therefore, was frustrated and it was this frustration which might have led her to suicide.
19.1 PW-1 in his cross-examination admitted that he had been taking Vandana to a Tantrik for magical cure.

The pertinent portion of his cross-examination recorded on 24.11.2021 is reproduced below for ready reference:
" I have no knowledge what is meant by ' Dinari', but it a kind of some magic spell (totka).
It is correct that I took my daughter to "Tantrik" who told me that she was suffering from 'Dinari' and he gave a cure for it."

19.2 PW-8 Vinod Bhadoria had deposed that he provided the record of diagnostic procedures conducted on Vandana during her life time by concerned experts, the opinion of these experts and the medication prescribed by them to Vandana.
These documents were seized by the IO and memorandum this seizure is Ex.PW-8/A.
This record is Ex.PW-8/B (colly. Running into 13 pages) .

On the fourth page of Ex.PW-8/B (colly) is the prescription drawn by Sparsh Hospital, Peeragarhi,
New Delhi for Vandana, on 10.07.2019.

The salient features of this document, relevant to the present case in light of the arguments of defence are :

sentences.text: The examining doctor who drew the prescription cited above found that Vandana needed to be evaluated for probable mental illness as he referred Vandana to a psychiatrist.
19.4 Thus, what appears from the material available on record is that deceased Vandana was not keeping well and she was exhibiting signs/symptoms of some mental illness too.
A person suffering from mental illness is expected to be drawn to commit suicide.
20. PW-2 Smt. Sona Devi is mother of the Vandana.
She is a failed witness.
She failed to prove any fact which would have assisted the prosecution to bring home the charge.
21. A suicide note was found at site as deposed by PW-5.
It was torn and the contents thereof were delineated by scribbling thereon
The FSL operated upon this document to decipher the shrouded contents.

21.1 From the above deciphered suicide noted Ex.PW-5/B, what can be culled out by objective assessment thereof is that deceased Vandana committed the act of suicide upon self propulsion being troubled while excusing and exonerating one and all from the burden of her act and it's consequence.

21.2 From the assessment of the available evidence, it is inferred that deceased Vandana was troubled by both or either of the two following conditions:
 i. by her ailments, or  ii. by the conduct of her in-laws 21.3
In considered opinion of this court, out of the two situations referred above, the evidence is suggestive that the primary cause of Vandana's trouble was her ailments.

Though the crests of exciting/elevating and troughs of frustrating/ troubling effects of natural sinusoidal behavioural interactions between husband and wife rooted in rigors of daily life may have accentuated the psychological impact of the ailments suffered by Vandana.
21.4 Hence, it cannot be presumed as required by the mandate of section 304 B IPC that the suicide committed by Vandana is 'dowry death'.

sentences.text: There is no positive evidence of cruelty or harassment as envisaged in Section 498A IPC in the material available on record.

There was no complaint of any cruelty or harassment made by deceased Vandana or her family members claiming to be offended by such cruelty or harassment, to any competent authority for redressal of such grievance, during the lifetime of Vandana.

Hence,
there is no evidence to consider/ believe the fact of cruelty committed on Vandana which could have led her to commit suicide.
22.1 There is no record of social media posts by Vandana expressing regrets from her marriage.

There is no record of messages sent by her neither whatsapp nor SMS, to her father, mother,
siblings, cousins, friends or acquaintances expressing her grief and complaint.
23. Hence, in considered opinion of this court, the prosecution has failed to prove it's case beyond reasonable doubt.
The accuseds - Dinesh Pratap, Rajpal Singh and Kamla are, therefore, acquitted of the charges.

The Ld. Magistrate committed the case to the Court of Sessions after compliance of the relevant provisions.
The incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against the accuseds were brought to their notice and their explanation was sought.
Accuseds claimed that they were innocent.
Accuseds opted to lead defence evidence,
however, by order dated 06.05.2025, defence evidence was closed as they could not produce any defence witness.
On 18.07.2019, Vandana committed suicide by hanging.
16.1 From the above referred facts, it is inferred that before death, Vandana was not intoxicated/
poisoned and that she was not subjected to physical violence of any sorts.
It is also sufficiently established that Vandana's death was not caused by burns or bodily injury.
17. It is proved that death of Vandana occurred within seven years of her marriage and that her death occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances; the deceased was married to A-1 on 18.04.2018 and she died on 18.07.2019 and her death was caused by asphyxia due to ante-mortem hanging.
18. The only ingredient of the offence punishable u/s 304B IPC which the prosecution was burdened with to prove, to successfully bring home the charge u/s 304 B IPC, was that soon before her death,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But, there is no deposition to the effect that to coerce the deceased or her family to satisfy this demand, the deceased was subjected to cruelty.
Furthermore, Vandana committed suicide on 18.07.2019 and this day cannot be said to be 'soon after' December-2018.
19.4 Thus, what appears from the material available on record is that deceased Vandana was not keeping well and she was exhibiting signs/symptoms of some mental illness too.
A person suffering from mental illness is expected to be drawn to commit suicide.
She is a failed witness.
21.1 From the above deciphered suicide noted Ex.PW-5/B, what can be culled out by objective assessment thereof is that deceased Vandana committed the act of suicide upon self propulsion being troubled while excusing and exonerating one and all from the burden of her act and it's consequence.
21.2 From the assessment of the available evidence, it is inferred that deceased Vandana was troubled by both or either of the two following conditions:
 i. by her ailments, or  ii. by the conduct of her in-laws 21.3
In considered opinion of this court, out of the two situations referred above, the evidence is suggestive that the primary cause of Vandana's trouble was her ailments.
Though the crests of exciting/elevating and troughs of frustrating/ troubling effects of natural sinusoidal behavioural interactions between husband and wife rooted in rigors of daily life may have accentuated the psychological impact of the ailments suffered by Vandana.
21.4 Hence, it cannot be presumed as required by the mandate of section 304 B IPC that the suicide committed by Vandana is 'dowry death'.

9 22.
There is no positive evidence of cruelty or harassment as envisaged in Section 498A IPC in the material available on record.
There was no complaint of any cruelty or harassment made by deceased Vandana or her family members claiming to be offended by such cruelty or harassment, to any competent authority for redressal of such grievance, during the lifetime of Vandana.
Hence,
there is no evidence to consider/ believe the fact of cruelty committed on Vandana which could have led her to commit suicide.
22.1 There is no record of social media posts by Vandana expressing regrets from her marriage.
There is no record of messages sent by her neither whatsapp nor SMS, to her father, mother,
siblings, cousins, friends or acquaintances expressing her grief and complaint.
23. Hence, in considered opinion of this court, the prosecution has failed to prove it's case beyond reasonable doubt.
